source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 21. Exercises reused from the lesson.
topic: Four hadiths on salah, zakah, fasting and hajj

learn.en: “Allah does not accept a salah without purification, or charity from money obtained by fraud.” (Muslim) — make wudu carefully and be honest with money.
learn.title: Clean prayer, clean money

learn.en: Whoever does not pay the zakah on his wealth will meet it on the Day of Resurrection as a fearsome snake saying “I am your wealth!” (Al-Bukhari) — zakah keeps money clean and helps people in need.
learn.title: Zakah is the right of the poor

learn.en: Every good deed is rewarded 10 to 700 times, but fasting is for Allah and He rewards it Himself. The fasting person has two joys: at iftar, and on meeting his Lord. (Muslim)
learn.title: Fasting is for Allah

learn.en: “A blessed pilgrimage has no reward but Paradise.” (Al-Bukhari) — a blessed hajj is done the Prophet's ﷺ way, with good manners and no anger.
learn.title: A blessed hajj

learn.en: “Nor does he speak from his own inclination. It is not but a revelation revealed.” (Qur'an 53:3-4)
learn.title: From the Qur'an

words.en: a hadith (saying of the Prophet ﷺ)

quiz.en: Allah does not accept salah without…
Good deeds are multiplied up to…
The reward of a blessed hajj is…
True or false? A fasting person has two joys.

think.q: Which of the four hadiths will you remember most, and why?
think.a: Each one teaches us to worship Allah the right way.

parents.summary: Four hadiths: no salah without purity, the warning for unpaid zakah, the special reward of fasting, and Paradise for a blessed hajj.
parents.tip: Learn one hadith's meaning per week and share it at dinner.
